transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-07-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sarah Blake (Helios Head of Data), Ravi Kapoor (Helios Infra), Nina Morales (Helios Product), James O'Connell (Helios Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress, access readiness (VPC/peering, IAM, firewall), preliminary bench numbers from Helios test harness, and next steps for a larger load run. Discussed a couple of integration/blocker items (outbound firewall to registry, missing S3 role for KV cache snapshots) and tuning knobs (batching, kv cache, quantization).

Topics covered:
- Onboarding status and open access tickets
- Initial performance observations and estimator differences
- Environment readiness: VPC peering, NAT, KMS access, service account roles
- Tuning suggestions (batch size, kv/prefix cache, model variant selection)
- Next steps and schedule for load tests and security docs

Action items called out in meeting (also in metadata): Lucas to run bench, Maya to send security docs, Ravi to unblock network, Nina to finalize criteria.

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription contains natural speech artifacts):
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick check — we've got about 45 minutes. Agenda: access, benches, blockers, next steps. Sound good?
[00:08] Sarah Blake: Yep all good. Ravi, you tuned in?
[00:11] Ravi Kapoor: Yeah I'm here, I can talk infra.
[00:13] Lucas Ortega: Hi, Lucas from the SE team. I pulled the small-run numbers you sent last night, Sarah — thanks.
[00:20] Sarah Blake: Sure. The harness ran about 200 requests with our real prompt mix. We attached the CSV in the drive.
[00:25] Maya Chen: Great. Quick housekeeping — did we get the VPC peering details from Helios side? I saw an open ticket.
[00:31] Ravi Kapoor: Ticket's open, I'm waiting on the network team to add the route table. There's also an issue with the company proxy — outbound to our container registry is blocked by default.
[00:40] Priya Nair: That proxy block will stop the private deployment image pull, yes. For hosted mode it's less relevant but for Dedicated or Private you need registry access and S3/KMS for snapshots.
[00:50] James O'Connell: We also need to confirm KMS access patterns. We have a PwC audit coming and need to ensure keys are customer-managed.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Yes, we support customer KMS/HSM — I'll include the architecture note in the docs.
[01:05] Nina Morales: On the bench numbers — we saw p95 around 420ms on your csv. Is that expected?
[01:12] Lucas Ortega: I looked at the CSV. A couple of caveats — your harness had batching disabled and sequence lengths averaged ~1,100. We ran earlier with a shorter context and saw p95 closer to ~260ms. The 420ms sounds like the longer seqs plus no kv cache.
[01:28] Sarah Blake: We did include multi-turns, so seq lengths spike. The app needs history for UX.
[01:34] Lucas Ortega: Totally — two suggestions: enable prefix/KV cache for repeated system prompts, and cap the max_history tokens we send to the model by truncating older turns. Both cut cost and latency.
[01:43] Ravi Kapoor: About KV cache — our security team is cautious about caching. Anything stored will need to be encrypted with our keys or we need to avoid persisting anything on shared disk.
[01:51] Maya Chen: Understood. We can configure cache to encrypt at rest with your KMS or use ephemeral in-memory cache. We'll list options in the config doc.
[01:58] Priya Nair: Also, quantization profiles — for throughput-focused workloads we recommended int8 for your model with minor quality checks. That reduced token compute in our tests by ~30% in the lab.
[02:09] Nina Morales: Would quantizing affect hallucination rates for our financial prompts?
[02:13] Lucas Ortega: There's a small delta sometimes. That's why we tie quality monitoring to a prompt set and do regression alerts. We'll run the same eval set after quant and compare.
[02:22] Maya Chen: Ok for the bench results itself — Lucas, can you summarize the key metrics we saw and differences between hosted vs dedicated?
[02:28] Lucas Ortega: Sure. From our internal quick-run: hosted (our hosted API) with model X-2.7, batch=1, seq~512 -> p95 ~230ms, avg token throughput ~180 tok/s. Dedicated with the same model on a mid-range GPU and batching=4 -> p95 ~180ms, throughput ~420 tok/s but added cold-start variability. Helios CSV had batching 0 and seq sometimes >1k which explains the higher p95 (420ms). Also cost per 1k tokens in hosted vs dedicated changes with utilization; we'll send a short cost model.
[02:54] Sarah Blake: That helps. Our main SLO is p95 < 300ms for user-facing flows, and a cost target of X per 1M tokens (we'll share exact number).
[03:05] Maya Chen: Cool — that p95 target is achievable with tuning and caching. blockers are mostly network and IAM. Ravi, the firewall/regulatory side?
[03:13] Ravi Kapoor: Firewall: we must allow outbound egress to Redwood registry and your hosted control plane IPs for onboarding. I'll open a ticket to whitelist the /24 you sent last week; need to confirm the exact IP range.
[03:22] Maya Chen: I'll resend the connectivity checklist right after this; it includes IP ranges and ports (registry, KMS, S3).
[03:30] James O'Connell: Also need a legible SOC2 package; our security team won't sign off without it.
[03:34] Maya Chen: Yep — I'll attach our SOC2 attestation, encryption docs, and an architecture whitepaper.
[03:39] Priya Nair: On integration steps — for the private deployment you need: VPC peering, NAT for outbound, KMS access, and a service account with s3:PutObject/GetObject for cache snapshots. For dedicated, you can skip registry pulls if we host the image in your private registry via our partner flow but that adds setup time.
[03:57] Nina Morales: How long does dedicated setup usually take once VPC peering is done?
[04:01] Lucas Ortega: Typically 2–3 business days for provisioning and testing assuming networking is clean. If we need an air-gapped on-prem install it's more like 2–3 weeks due to approvals.
[04:10] Sarah Blake: For this POC we prefer Hosted first, then dedicated if cost/perf swing in our favor.
[04:15] Maya Chen: Makes sense. We'll run two tracks: hosted quick test + dedicated smoke once network is ready.
[04:21] Ravi Kapoor: Quick Q — the SSO integration, can we do SAML with our Okta?
[04:25] Maya Chen: Yes, SAML/Okta supported. We'll include the SSO guide in the doc bundle.
[04:30] James O'Connell: Favorite question — audit logs retention? Can you keep detailed audit trails for model prompts?
[04:36] Priya Nair: We store audit logs in the console and can configure retention (30/90/365 days) depending on plan. For Private deployments logs can be shipped to your SIEM.
[04:45] Sarah Blake: Great. One more on the bench CSV: there's a couple of outliers where latency spikes above 1.2s. Can we dig into those?
[04:51] Lucas Ortega: Likely cold-start or large seqs in that sample. In the next run please include a column for seq_length and batch_size; that'll help attribute. Also indicate whether the run used kv cache.
[04:59] Maya Chen: We'll request a reproducible short script from Helios so we run the same harness. That helps compare apples-to-apples.
[05:06] Nina Morales: When do you want the reproducible harness?
[05:09] Maya Chen: If you can drop it in the drive by EOD tomorrow we can run the 1,000-query bench on Friday.
[05:14] Sarah Blake: I'll try to get that in tonight.
[05:16] Maya Chen: Cool. Final recap: Lucas runs bench and posts results (due Fri 7/18), Maya sends SOC2/conn docs tomorrow (7/16), Ravi to unblock network (7/17), Nina to finalize SLOs/cost target (7/20). We'll schedule the load test for week of 7/21 pending those items.
[05:32] Ravi Kapoor: One small note — our infra team wants to confirm whether Redwood stores any PII in logs by default.
[05:37] Priya Nair: By default we do not persist PII; logs are request metadata only, prompts are not retained in hosted unless configured for evals. We'll document retention and redaction options.
[05:44] Sarah Blake: Ok thanks. Anything else?
[05:46] Maya Chen: Nope — appreciate the time. We'll follow up in email and update the ticket list.
[05:50] Nina Morales: Thanks everyone.
[05:52] End meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: Automated transcription had some mis-attributions (Speaker labels swapped in a few segments) and occasional homophone errors ("KV cache" transcribed as "KV cash" in one spot), edited minimally for readability but preserved stutters and filler words.

Links referenced in call: Shared drive (drive.redwood.example/hel-POC), SOC2 attestation (link to doc), bench CSV (drive.redwood.example/hel-POC/benches.csv), connectivity checklist (drive.redwood.example/hel-POC/connectivity.pdf)
